text:
Hemoglobin contains $0.34%$ of iron by mass. The number of Fe atoms in $3.3\mathrm{g}$ of hemoglobin is

(Given: Atomic mass of Fe is $56\quad \mathrm{u},\mathrm{N}_{\mathrm{A}}=6.022\times 10^{23}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Iron is $0.34%$ of the mass of hemoglobin, so the mass of iron in $3.3\text{g}$ of hemoglobin is

$m_{\mathrm{Fe}}=\dfrac{0.34}{100}\times 3.3=1.122\times 10^{-2}\text{g}$

Moles of iron:

$n_{\mathrm{Fe}}=\dfrac{1.122\times 10^{-2}}{56}=2.004\times 10^{-4}\text{mol}$

Number of Fe atoms:

$N=n_{\mathrm{Fe}}\times N_{A}=2.004\times 10^{-4}\times 6.022\times 10^{23}=1.21\times 10^{20}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text:
Arrange the following in increasing order of their covalent character.

A. $\mathrm{CaF}_{2}$

B. $\mathrm{CaCl}_{2}$

C. $\mathrm{CaBr}_{2}$

D. $\mathrm{CaI}_{2}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From Fajan's rule, for a given metal ion, as the size of anion increases, polarizability of anion increases and hence covalent character of the given ionic compound increases.

Hence, the increasing order of covalent character is $\mathrm{CaF}_{2}<\mathrm{CaCl}_{2}<\mathrm{CaBr}_{2}<\mathrm{CaI}_{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text:
Class XII students were asked to prepare one litre of buffer solution of $\mathrm{pH}8.26$ by their Chemistry teacher. The amount of ammonium chloride to be dissolved by the student in $0.2\mathrm{M}$ ammonia solution to make one litre of the buffer is :

(Given: $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})=4.74$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{NH}_{3}=17\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}=53.5\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For basic Buffer, $\mathrm{pOH}=\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{b}}+\log \frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{Base}]}$

$\mathrm{pOH}=14-8.26=5.74$

$5.74=4.74+\log \frac{[\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}]}{0.2}$

$[\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}]=2\mathrm{M}$

Moles of $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}=2\times 1=2$ moles

Weight of $\mathrm{NH}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}=2\times 53.5=107\mathrm{g}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text:
At $30^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$, the half life for the decomposition of $\mathrm{AB}_{2}$ is $200\mathrm{s}$ and is independent of the initial concentration of $\mathrm{AB}_{2}$. The time required for $80%$ of the $\mathrm{AB}_{2}$ to decompose is

Given: $\log 2=0.30$ $\log 3=0.48$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since, half-life is independent of the initial concentration of $AB_{2}$. Hence, the reaction is "First Order".

$k=\frac{2.303\log 2}{t_{1/2}}$

$\frac{2.303\log 2}{t_{1/2}}=\frac{2.303}{t}\log \frac{100}{(100-80)}$

$\frac{2.303\times 0.3}{200}=\frac{2.303}{t}\log 5$

$t=467\mathrm{s}$

text: The metal complex that is diamagnetic is (Atomic number: $\mathrm{Fe},26;\mathrm{Cu},29)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Oxidation states follow from the charge on each complex ion, with $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ each $-1$.

In $\mathrm{K}{}_{3}[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]$, Cu is $+1$. Cu is $[\text{Ar}]3d^{10}4s^{1}$, so $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{+}$ is $[\text{Ar}]3d^{10}$ with every electron paired: diamagnetic.

In $\mathrm{K}{}_{2}[\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]$, Cu is $+2$, i.e. $3d^{9}$, with one unpaired electron: paramagnetic.

In $\mathrm{K}{}_{3}[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]$, Fe is $+1$ with 25 electrons; an odd number of electrons leaves at least one unpaired: paramagnetic.

In $\mathrm{K}{}_{4}[\mathrm{FeCl}{}_{6}]$, Fe is $+2$, i.e. $3d^{6}$; $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ is a weak-field ligand, so the complex is high spin, $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$, with 4 unpaired electrons: paramagnetic.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

The correct sequential order of the reagents for the given reaction is

solution.body:

Fe/$\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ then reduces $-\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ to $-\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$; $\mathrm{HNO}{}_{2}$ diazotises this new amino group, and warming the diazonium salt with water replaces $-\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ by OH, giving 4-iodophenol.

In (A) and (D) the nitro group is reduced before the first diazonium group is replaced by I, and in (C) the second $\mathrm{HNO}{}_{2}$ is added before there is an amino group to diazotise.

options: Both $𝐀$ and $𝐑$ are true and $𝐑$ is the correct explanation of $𝐀$.
Both $𝐀$ and $𝐑$ are true but $𝐑$ is NOT the correct explanation of $𝐀$.

solution.body:

text: Consider an imaginary ion ${}_{22}^{48}\mathrm{X}^{3-}$. The nucleus contains '$a$'% more neutrons than the number of electrons in the ion. The value of 'a' is $_______________$. [nearest integer]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Number of electrons in ${}_{22}^{48}X^{3-}$ is 25 .

Number of neutrons $=48-22=26$.

$%$ increase in the number of neutrons over electrons

$=\left (\frac{26-25}{25}\right )100=4%$

$\therefore a=4$

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Molality of a solution of non volatile solute $(A)=1$

 Elevation in boiling point is given by

$\Delta \mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{b}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}\mathrm{m}$

$3=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}\times 1$         ... (1)

Molality of $(A)$ in the same solvent $=2$

text: Total number of isomers (including stereoisomers) obtained on monochlorination of methylcyclohexane is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Methylcyclohexane has five kinds of hydrogen (on the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ group and on ring carbons C1, C2, C3 and C4), so monochlorination gives five structural isomers.


[IMG]

(Chloromethyl)cyclohexane: no stereocentre: 1.

1-Chloro-1-methylcyclohexane: C1 carries two identical ring paths, so there is no stereocentre: 1.

1-Chloro-2-methylcyclohexane: C1 and C2 are both stereocentres and neither isomer has a plane of symmetry, so cis and trans each exist as a pair of enantiomers: 4.

1-Chloro-3-methylcyclohexane: C1 and C3 are both stereocentres (the two ring paths from each are unequal) and neither isomer has a plane of symmetry, so cis and trans each exist as a pair of enantiomers: 4.

1-Chloro-4-methylcyclohexane: a plane through C1, C4, Cl and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ makes both isomers achiral, so only cis and trans exist: 2.

Total number of isomers $=1+1+4+4+2=12$.

Hence, the answer is 12.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift

text: A $100\mathrm{mL}$ solution of $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{MgBr}$ on treatment with methanol produces $2.24\mathrm{mL}$ of a gas at STP. The weight of gas produced is $_____________ mg$. [nearest integer]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 26th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{MgBr}+\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{OH}\to \mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}+\mathrm{MgBr}(\mathrm{OCH}_{3})$

As $2.24\mathrm{ml}$ is formed at STP.

Number of moles of ethane gas produced

$=\frac{2.24X}{22.4}$

$=10^{-4}\mathrm{ml}$

Mass of ethane produced $=10^{-4}\times 30=3\times 10^{-}=3\mathrm{mg}$
